project_scope: Assistive, non-diagnostic quantitative analysis of the left ventricle from A4C echocardiography.
test_partition_note: The test partition was excluded from the clean Phase 1A-1D model-selection experiments and from Phase 2A quantitative-method selection. However, because this partition had historical pilot exposure, it is not described as a pristine external test set.

quantitative_pipeline.physical_measurement: Original NIfTI pixel spacing adjusted separately in x and y for stretch-resize scaling.
quantitative_pipeline.LV_area: binary LV cavity area in mm^2

EF_error_decomposition.important_note: These error components are not additive because signed errors may interact or partially cancel.

image_quality_analysis.interpretation: Segmentation-induced EF error increased descriptively from Good to Medium to Poor image quality. The Poor subgroup contained only seven patients, so this analysis is considered descriptive rather than definitive.

area.alternative: ES absolute relative error > ED absolute relative error

volume.alternative: ESV absolute relative error > EDV absolute relative error

paired_ED_vs_ES_analysis.interpretation: Within this 50-patient evaluation sample, ES-related area and volume errors were greater than the corresponding ED errors under the predefined paired analysis.

failure_case_analysis.selection: Three patients with the largest absolute GT-geometry to predicted-geometry EF disagreement.
failure_case_analysis.observed_pattern: All three high-error cases showed ED cavity underestimation, while ES was either only slightly different or substantially overestimated. This asymmetric ED/ES error reduced the estimated ED-to-ES volume change and produced substantial EF underestimation.
failure_case_analysis.image_quality_observation: The three cases included one Good, one Medium, and one Poor quality scan, showing that large downstream errors were not confined to poor-quality images.
failure_case_analysis.interpretation_limit: These cases were deliberately selected as the largest errors and are not representative samples of the entire evaluation cohort.

main_findings: The frozen segmentation masks enabled extraction of physically scaled LV area, PCA long-axis length, EDV, ESV, SV and EF.
ES measurements were more sensitive to segmentation error than ED measurements.
ES area absolute relative error was 9.48% compared with 6.88% at ED.
ESV absolute relative error was 15.48% compared with 11.88% for EDV.
The paired ED/ES analysis supported greater ES-related error for both area and volume within this evaluation sample.
Predicted masks showed systematic underestimation of LV area and area-length volume on average.
GT-to-predicted EF bias was close to zero despite volume underestimation because ED and ES errors can partially cancel in the EF ratio.
Near-zero mean EF bias did not imply patient-level agreement; GT-to-predicted EF 95% limits of agreement were approximately -14.87 to +15.07 percentage points.
Ground-truth-mask geometry itself differed materially from CAMUS reference EF, indicating that total end-to-end EF disagreement cannot be attributed solely to segmentation.
Failure analysis demonstrated that asymmetric ED/ES segmentation errors can propagate nonlinearly into large EF errors.
limitations: The volume calculation uses a simplified single-plane A4C area-length approximation.
GT-mask-derived geometric EDV, ESV and EF are internal geometric comparators and are not equivalent to direct clinical ground-truth measurements.
CAMUS Info_4CH.cfg provides reference EF but does not provide corresponding reference EDV and ESV values for direct absolute volume validation.
The Poor image-quality subgroup contains only seven patients.
The final evaluation partition had historical pilot exposure and is therefore not considered a pristine external test set.
CAMUS does not contain longitudinal repeated visits for these patients, so this phase does not validate true longitudinal change tracking.
